title: Real Euclidean Lebesgue integral
statement: Use $\mathbf R$ [def-weil-field]. For an integer $m\geq0$, write $\mathbf R^m=(\operatorname{Fin}(m)\to\mathbf R)$ with its Borel measurable structure, and let $\lambda_m$ be the finite product of the usual real Lebesgue measures, one for each coordinate (the empty product measure when $m=0$). For a function $f:\mathbf R^m\to\mathbf R$, define $\int_{\mathbf R^m} f(z)\,dz$ to be its real Bochner integral with respect to $\lambda_m$: the integral of its $L^1$ equivalence class when $f$ is integrable, and $0$ otherwise. Here integrable means almost everywhere strongly measurable with $\int\|f\|\,d\lambda_m<\infty$. This is a total real-valued operation on functions; in the integrable case it is the usual signed Lebesgue integral.
